messages.subject: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
messages.subject_clean: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I am trying to model density of jaguars by different years (3) and I first run the detection and sigma to get the best models. Then I created 3 different masks for each session (years).
Problem is when I tried the different models for density, it just end up giving me the same exact values for all models and not getting into consideration the Density part of it. I have the feeling that it may be due to the way I am adding the mask but I am not sure as it is the first time I'm doing it.
Here is the code from the mask part on:

mask_1<-read.mask("Mask_1s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
mask_2<-read.mask("Mask_2s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
mask_3<-read.mask("Mask_3s.csv", spacing = 500, header=TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))

mask=list("Sess1" =mask_1,"Sess2" =mask_2,"Sess3" =mask_3)

All_Jag=MS.capthist(Sess1,Sess2,Sess3)
summary(All_Jag, terse = TRUE)

fits6a <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~1,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6b <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~NDVI,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6c <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~dWater,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))
fits6d <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~NDVI+dWater,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE))

AicsJagD1=AIC(fits6a,fits6b,fits6c,fits6d)
AicsJagD1

First of this I was trying a different way for the masks but was getting a warning and still the same values for all models. Now I don't get warnings but still the same result.

mask_1<-read.csv("Mask_1s.csv")
mask1<-read.mask(data=mask_1, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)

mask_2<-read.csv("Mask_2s.csv")
mask2<-read.mask(data=mask_2, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)
mask_3<-read.csv("Mask_3s.csv")
mask3<-read.mask(data=mask_3, spacing = 500, header=TRUE)

msk1=read.mask(data=mask1,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
msk2=read.mask(data=mask2,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))
msk3=read.mask(data=mask3,spacing = 500, header = TRUE,columns=c("NDVI","dWater"))

mask=list(msk1,msk2,msk3)

All_Jag=MS.capthist(Sess1,Sess2,Sess3)
summary(All_Jag, terse = TRUE)

fits6a <- secr.fit(All_Jag,model=list(D~1,g0~Prey,sigma~session),mask=mask, trace = FALSE,verify=FALSE,CL=TRUE,details = list(fastproximity = FALSE,contrasts = list(session = MASS::contr.sdif)))

#WARNING
#1: In model.matrix.default(formula, data = data, contrasts.arg = contrasts) :
  #variable 'session' is absent, its contrast will be ignored

Can someone please give me some light in what I am doing wrong?
Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
messages.subject_clean: Problem with density fit, mask and its covariates
messages.body_plain:
Hello Bardales

I assume you surveyed substantially different areas in the three years, or the covariates changed between years. If you surveyed essentially the same area and covariates did not change then I would use the same mask to save some of the messing about.

You cannot model density (D ~ NDVI etc.) in a conditional model (CL = TRUE) (incidentally, it would be easier to read the code if you used spaces).
I suggest dropping the whole 'details' argument at least for a start - I don't see why you cannot use the fastproximity method, and contrasts.arg is giving trouble. (The handling of contrasts did change recently so there may be a real issue there, but let's strip out unnecessary stuff).

Regards
Murray

messages.subject: Beta parameters, positively associated or negatively?
messages.subject_clean: Beta parameters, positively associated or negatively?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I've had a inhomogeneous model with some covariates of density. And I'd like to know whether density is positively or negatively associated with those covariates.

I'm able to fit a regression of density ~ covariates by ggplot, but sometimes the goodness of fitting is not so good and the relationship is unclear (whether positive or negative).

In a secr study by Oberosler et al. 2021, it is said that:

"The best model included slope as positively and signifcantly associated to density (βSlope= 1.44 [95% CI: 0.66–2.21])."

It seems like by looking at beta parameters of covariates, we can tell that the density is positively correlated with covariates if beta>0, and vise versa. Is that true?

I can access betas by coef(), and the result is:

                   beta
D               -9.8066215558
D.cov1       0.1274173635
D.cov2       0.5090616878
D.cov3      -0.0781366258
D.factor1   0.5192772418
D.factor2   2.0800721325

But I'm unsure whether I should backtransform these betas before I tell the relationship between density and covariates, or I don't have to?

e.g., here beta cov3 is negative, so density is slightly and negatively correlated with cov3? But after backtransform, beta cov3 will be positive.

If I need to backtransform, should I use inverse log or inverse logit?

Also, if I'm going to have covariates of g0 or sigma, do things work in the same way?

It might be a simple (even stupid) question. but I've been struggling to find the answer. Thank you very much!

messages.subject: Re: Beta parameters, positively associated or negatively?
messages.subject_clean: Beta parameters, positively associated or negatively?
messages.body_plain:
Hi
The sign of the beta coefficients gives you the direction of the relationship. No need to back transform, and in fact it is meaningless to backtransform a single coefficient. The coefficient gives the slope of the relationship on the relevant link scale (defaults log for density, logit for g0 and log for sigma). Another (better) way to test for an effect is to compare models with and without that covariate (e.g. with a likelihood ratio test see ?LR.test).
Murray

messages.subject: Home range area estimation with camera traps via secr
messages.subject_clean: Home range area estimation with camera traps via secr
messages.body_plain:
Dear all secr users,

I am using camera traps data to perform secr models. I have 4 different chimpanzee communities, and I wanted to see if I could estimate the home range of each group thanks to the results of the secr model (and the estimation of sigma).

>From what I gather through reading, home range area is possible to obtain using the value of sigma, if gaussian encounter probability model is used. The best AIC model was the MBk one, I used the half normal key function, and computed the 95% territory usage via the calculus pi*(sigma*sqrt(5.99))^2. (Chapter 5 of the secr book from 2014).

In this chapter, on the wolverine example, the authors though advise against biological interpretations of home range area based on the sigma estimate from SECR. From what I understand it could be misleading if the traps affect the individuals use patterns, which I assume is not the case in my study. I will still treat those home range area estimates with cautions but thought this would be more relevant than MCP that is fully constrained by my camera array. I wonder if anyone has any thoughts on the matter.

Furthermore, I would like to be able to map those home range areas. I used the function fxi.contour on all my individuals to get a “space use” for each of my individuals in one group. I checked what happened if I set the fxi.contour percentage at 100%. I am obtaining a very big area by overlaying all the polygon from each individual extracted from the fxi.contour results.

The blue dots are the cameras, and they cover an area of 10 km x 10 km.

I then decided to try to understand what was happening and had a look at each individual space use estimated via fxi.contour.

On this second figure (only a subsample of all individuals), blue points are still camera, green points are the camera where the specific individual has been captured and on the title is of each graph the name of the individual and the number of times we captured them. The big red dot is the home range center.

 I directly noticed that the more captured an individual has been, the more tighten around the home range center the results of the fxi.contour was. For the individuals with more than 2 captures (top middle and right, Cybele and Phine) the results are circle very closed to the home range center with even some cameras where they have been captured not included in that area.

I assume I should not take the 100% data, but I was wondering as the number of captures is affecting the size of the “space use” if there was a recommendation on having only a certain number of captures to be able to perform fxi.contour function on individuals (obviously 1 capture individuals should not be used but 2 times capture individuals also give unrealistic results). And I also wondered if the results on fxi.contour with some restrictions on capture frequency could be used the way I showed above to determine an home range area for my different groups. If not, would there be another way to access the territory of my different groups via the results of the secr model?

Any advice on the matter would be greatly appreciated!

Best regards,

Benjamin Debetencourt

messages.subject: Re: Home range area estimation with camera traps via secr
messages.subject_clean: Home range area estimation with camera traps via secr
messages.body_plain:
Hello Benjamin
One basic point: fxi.contour and related functions do not describe space use at all. The contours are for the location of an animal's activity centre, given the data and the model. They always become tighter with more sampling (maybe not quite 'always' but that is how it should work).
The relationship between (halfnormal) sigma and 95% home range size is obviously coarse and subject to all sorts of hedging - useful as a ballpark figure but not much else. It doesn't let you plot each home range on a map. There has been some unpublished work combining sigma (as an indication of space use) and fxi-type statistics (a talk at the vNCSE conference by Rishika Chopara, from memory), but I'm not sure how far that has gone.
Murray

messages.subject: newdata argument for model averaging
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I tried to use "newdata" inside "modelAverage" (openCR), however, the output only shows the first level of the cofactor.

I put together an example with the issue, using the "modelAverage" example from the manual.

I would very much appreciate any help!!

Thank you in advance!
Lukas

#The newdata model averaging example:

library(openCR) #load library

## Compare two models fitted previously

cjs1 <- openCR.fit(dipperCH, model=p~sex)
cjs2 <- openCR.fit(dipperCH, model=p~session+sex)
AIC(cjs1, cjs2)

#model averaging using "newdata" to show male and female estimates
modelAverage(cjs1, cjs2,
                   newdata=expand.grid(session=1:7, sex = factor(c('Male','Female'))))

The newdata argument needs factors (no numbers) and the object needs to be an openCR list.

Best,
Lukas

Here is the - now working - former example:

library(openCR) #load library

## Compare two models fitted previously

cjs1 <- openCR.fit(dipperCH, model=p~sex)
cjs2 <- openCR.fit(dipperCH, model=p~session+sex)
AIC(cjs1, cjs2)

#make it into a list
cjs12 <- openCRlist(cjs1, cjs2)

#model averaging using "newdata" to show male and female estimates

NEW<-data.frame(expand.grid(session=1:7, sex = factor(c("Female","Male"))))
NEW[] <- lapply(NEW, factor)  #convert to factor
modelAverage(cjs12, newdata=NEW)

messages.subject: Re: newdata argument for model averaging
messages.body_plain:
Good that you made progress. I was still looking. There is a bug in modelAverage.openCR (it fails to pass arguments to modelAverage.openCRlist) but the workaround is to form an openCRlist yourself, as you found. 'session' is a factor, but other components of newdata may not be. So better is

modelAverage(openCRlist(cjs1, cjs2),
    newdata = expand.grid(session = factor(1:7), sex = factor(c('Male','Female'))))

modelAverage() needs more testing.
Murray

messages.subject: kernel values for females and males
messages.subject_clean: kernel values for females and males
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am running open pop spatially explicit models, using JSSAsecrlCL with openCR package, for seven ocelot surveys. The best fitted model, according to AICc, has the following parameters:

lambda0~Sex, phi~Sex, l~1, sigma~Sex, move.a~Sex

Move.a parameter is really different for females and for males.
To report the kernel values, I am using the function "make.kernel", but the values I get back are values for females only. How can I extract the values for males? Any idea?
Thank you very much
Best
Paula

messages.subject: Re: kernel values for females and males
messages.subject_clean: kernel values for females and males
messages.body_plain:
make.kernel() can be used with various inputs. You are applying it to an existing openCR model, in which case make.kernel internally calls predict.openCR(movementmodel,...) to determine the parameter(s) of the kernel. You should be able to pass covariates with the dots argument:
kF <- make.kernel(fit, newdata = data.frame(session = 1, Sex = 'F'))
kM <- make.kernel(fit, newdata = data.frame(session = 1, Sex = 'M'))
But I haven't tested this.

If that fails, you can simply call make.kernel with appropriate values
make.kernel(movementmodel = 'BVE', move.a = X, ...)
where X is the value for females or males from predict(fit) and ... includes other named arguments as specified (or default) in your original model.
Murray
